article.headline: Giving a Coding Agent Eyes Transforms Its Visual Output
article.lede: An AI that can see what it has built writes better code than one working blind. Peter Gostev's side-by-side comparison — the same prompt, the same model, one run with live browser vision and one without — makes that gap concrete. The subject is a *Three.js* voxel scene of San Francisco Bay, and the difference is not subtle.
article.body:
The task was to generate an interactive browser scene depicting the Golden Gate Bridge, the Marin Headlands, and surrounding bay in voxel form — blocky, Minecraft-style 3D geometry rendered in real time via *Three.js*, the JavaScript library that handles low-level WebGL so developers don't have to. The prompt went to OpenAI's Codex coding agent running GPT-5.4 at its "xHigh" compute setting, a tier suggesting extended reasoning or inference time (the precise meaning is not documented in the available sources).

The difference between the two outputs lies in a tool called the **Interactive Playwright Skill**. *Playwright* is a browser-automation framework originally built by Microsoft: it can launch a browser, load a page, click elements, take screenshots, and report what it sees. The skill harnesses that capability so the AI doesn't merely emit code and hand it back — it runs the code, looks at the live result through a screenshot, and revises. That loop is sometimes called *computer use*: the model treating a rendered UI as sensory input rather than relying solely on its trained intuition about what code should produce.

The output produced with the skill is markedly richer. The OCR from Gostev's screenshot shows the first scene includes bridge towers, cable sweeps, vertical hangers, terrain massing, ferries, a skyline hint, Alcatraz, whales, birds, and shoreline foam — along with interactive controls for fog density, traffic, wave energy, time of day, a cutaway X-ray mode, and a tilt-shift camera. The version generated without the skill is described as missing many of these elements and lacking coherence.

This illustrates a structural limitation that has nagged text-to-code AI since its earliest versions: the model learns from code but cannot directly perceive the visual output of that code. For logic-heavy work — an API endpoint, a sorting function — that gap rarely matters. For anything that renders pixels, it matters enormously. The Playwright loop closes that gap by giving the model genuine perceptual feedback, letting it catch omitted geometry or broken layout the way a human would by simply looking.

Whether this pattern generalises cleanly to other visual UI tasks remains to be seen; the demo is a single, admittedly striking example. But the principle is clear enough: agentic code generation improves when the agent can observe consequences, not just emit text.

concepts.definition: A capability in which an AI model takes screenshots of a running application and uses what it sees to guide its next actions — clicking, typing, or in this case revising code. It extends language models into the visual domain without requiring custom vision training on every UI.

An open-source browser automation library from Microsoft. It launches real browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) under programmatic control, enabling scripts — or AI agents — to load pages, interact with elements, and capture screenshots of live rendered output.

Short for volumetric pixel: the 3D equivalent of a pixel, representing a fixed-size cube in a three-dimensional grid. Voxel graphics give scenes a blocky, layered aesthetic; the style is familiar from games like Minecraft and is well-suited to procedural generation.

A JavaScript library that wraps WebGL, the browser's low-level 3D graphics API, into a friendlier set of abstractions for scenes, cameras, lights, and geometry. It is the standard tool for building interactive 3D content that runs directly in a browser tab.

A pattern in which an AI model executes a step, observes the outcome, and then decides whether to revise or continue. Rather than producing a single output and stopping, the model iterates — approximating the edit-run-inspect cycle a human developer follows.

repos.summary: Playwright is Microsoft's cross-browser automation library for Node.js, Python, Java, and .NET. It controls Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit browsers programmatically, supporting clicks, form fills, screenshots, and network interception. AI coding agents use it as a perception layer: launch the app, screenshot it, feed the image back to the model.

Three.js is the dominant JavaScript library for 3D graphics in the browser, abstracting WebGL into manageable scene graphs, camera controls, and material systems. It is widely used for data visualisations, product configurators, and generative art. The Golden Gate voxel scene in the post is built on top of it.
